title: Monotonicity of the endpoint threshold log ratio
statement: Let $f$ be a monotone, nonconstant Boolean function on a finite sign cube, and let $p_c,b\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $0<p_c<\tfrac12$ and $\tfrac12\le b<1$. If the biased-minus probability polynomial of $f$ has value $\tfrac12$ at $p_c$, then the function $p\mapsto -\log(1-B_f(p))+\tfrac12\log(1-p)$ is monotone on $[\tfrac12,b]$, where $B_f$ denotes that polynomial.
hypotheses_covered: biased-minus probability polynomial of f at p_c equals 1/2
caveat: The supplied statement does not include the definition of monotonicity on the sign cube or the construction of the biased-minus probability polynomial.
